email_subject: Application - Junior Brand Manager at Landing
email_body:
Dear Landing team,

I'm applying for the Junior Brand Manager role in Ghent. Your posting asks for someone who enjoys figuring out why something works and then making it work better — that's most of what I do.

As a freelance SEO and AI-search specialist and Junior Digital Marketer at Episto, I run on-page SEO and content for client sites, track results in Google Analytics, Search Console, Semrush and Ahrefs, and turn those numbers into changes that move organic traffic. I've also built and maintained Shopify stores for clothing brands harwindtf.com and custompremiumshirt.com — store design, catalogue, blog content.

I'm based in Zwijndrecht, close to Ghent. English is fluent, my Dutch is developing (writing B1, speaking A2+) and I'm working on it. I'd like to bring my reporting habits and hands-on attitude to your team.

Best regards,
Baver Ok

cover_letter:
Dear Landing team,

Junior Brand Manager at Landing — I'll be honest, the line that caught me was "attitude matters more than a perfect CV." Here's mine, and here's why I think it fits.

I work where SEO, content and web meet: currently as a Junior Digital Marketer at Episto and as a freelancer, handling on-page SEO, keyword research and content for client websites. That means I spend my days in Semrush, Ahrefs, Google Analytics and Search Console — watching what a page or a campaign does, working out why, and changing something to see if it performs better. Reporting on results and turning them into clear recommendations is already the core of my job, not something I'd be learning from scratch.

The fashion side isn't new either. I've designed and maintained Shopify stores for two clothing brands, harwindtf.com and custompremiumshirt.com: building the store, managing the product catalogue and writing the blog content. Apparel e-commerce taught me how quickly a product page, a photo or a line of copy changes what people buy — and how closely you have to watch the numbers to know which one it was.

I'm organised because freelancing demands it: several clients, several deadlines, nobody checking up on me. I take initiative because I've had to — I built and run baverok.com myself, hand-coded the landing page and set up the enquiry flow. What I want next is what your posting describes: a small team where I can learn from senior people, grow fast, and do real work for brands I actually like.

One honest note: my English is fluent and my Turkish is native, but my Dutch is a work in progress — writing B1, speaking A2+, and improving.

I'd enjoy meeting you in Ghent and hearing how you and your clients work together week to week.

Kind regards,
Baver Ok
